clue.text: Former lover was modelling, laid bare

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
a model posed for the artist or camera

explanation.surface: An old flame turns out to have been a nude model.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uncovered and left open to view has been stripped bare.

clue.text: Rome ripe to be changed? One's got rid of Caesar, perhaps

indicators.note: to be changed means the letters of Rome ripe are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, which is removed from the mix

explanation.surface: Rome is ready for change now a leader has disposed of Caesar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got rid of' says I leaves the jumble of ROMERIPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Several Caesars were Roman rulers with the imperial title, so Caesar is an example.

clue.text: Sow plus hog — one finds them on a farm

definitions.text: one finds them on a farm

indicators.note: to sow is to scatter seed, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A female pig plus a hog: farmyard animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sow' looks like a pig but works as the verb, to scatter.
explanation.definitionFit: Farm machines that turn over soil are a common sight on agricultural land.

clue.text: That woman will peel outside

parts.note: she is the pronoun for that woman
'll is the contracted form of will

explanation.surface: A woman intends to go and peel something outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard outer casing of a nut or egg is its protective covering.

clue.text: Find out, from Parisian, word in English

parts.note: de is French for from
a term is a word or expression

explanation.surface: Discovering a French word that is used in English.
explanation.definitionFit: To establish or ascertain the facts is to settle them by finding out.

clue.text: Embarrassed when actor initially exploits director

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'
a ham is an overacting performer

indicators.note: initially means take only the opening letter of exploits

explanation.surface: A performer feels shame on seeing a director take advantage of him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' picks the E of exploits, which sits between HAM and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe feeling awkward shame or discomfort over something.

clue.text: Friendship from a year in American university? Just the opposite

indicators.note: Just the opposite reverses the stated 'year in university', so the university goes into a and year

parts.note: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: Friendships made during a year at an American college.
explanation.definitionFit: Peaceful goodwill between people or nations is a state of friendly relations.

clue.text: Present: finest lotion

parts.note: to hand something over is to present it
the cream is the best part, the finest

explanation.surface: A gift of top-quality lotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A moisturiser for the skin of the fingers and palms is a kind of lotion.

clue.text: Coach finds skirt almost ruined

parts.note: a mini is a very short skirt

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word for ruined is dropped

parts.note: bust can mean broken or ruined

explanation.surface: A sports coach discovers a skirt has been nearly destroyed.
explanation.definitionFit: A coach is a road vehicle carrying passengers, and a small such vehicle fits.

clue.text: Wanted something done about gentleman

indicators.note: about says the act goes around the gentleman

parts.note: a deed is an act, something done
sir is a title or form of address for a gentleman

explanation.surface: A gentleman is wanted for some act he committed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something longed for or wished for is what someone wanted.

clue.text: Re stoop — it could make you most short

indicators.note: the letters of the two words could be rearranged to make something new

explanation.surface: Bending over makes you look shorter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' here means short of money, not small in height.
explanation.definitionFit: Being short of cash is being poor, so the most short is the most impoverished.

clue.text: Turn to bat — proceeds to lose wicket

indicators.note: to lose says a letter must be dropped from the word for proceeds

parts.note: winnings are the money taken in, the proceeds
W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: A cricket picture: a batsman's turn ends when a wicket falls.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an innings is a side's or player's spell batting.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, a player's spell at the crease is called an innings.

clue.text: Man in services seen with empty lorry on a frequent basis

parts.note: a regular is a professional soldier, as opposed to a reservist

indicators.note: empty means the middle of lorry is removed, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: A soldier is often spotted beside an unloaded truck.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done at frequent, even intervals happens habitually or often.

clue.text: Be in crate that's tossed north of the border?

definitions.text: that's tossed north of the border?

indicators.note: in tells us the word be goes inside the word for crate

parts.note: crate is slang for an old car
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something being thrown about inside a packing box in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'north of the border' means Scotland, where tossing the caber (a tree trunk) is a Highland Games event; crate is slang for a battered car.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish Highland Games feature tossing a long wooden pole, an event named after it.

clue.text: Grew small flowers

parts.note: rose is the past tense of rise, meaning grew
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Someone grew some tiny blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: These are a popular garden bloom, so they are an example of flowers.

clue.text: Where one finds doctors rise up and rise anew

parts.note: to surge is to rise up suddenly

indicators.note: anew says the second rise is made again in a new order

explanation.surface: Doctors rebel, rising up again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a GP's practice premises are called a surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a doctor's consulting rooms are a surgery, so doctors are found there.

clue.text: One thousand newspapers: editor's overwhelmed

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
the press is newspapers collectively
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: An editor is swamped by a thousand newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: To be deeply struck or awed by something is to be bowled over by it.

clue.text: Drop safety equipment

definitions.meaning: to drop someone or something from an aircraft by canopy
a canopy harness worn by skydivers to slow a fall

explanation.definitionFit: The device slows a falling body, and as a verb it means to deliver by air.

clue.text: Lingerie — two articles from abroad are ordered by women

parts.note: un is a French article, the indefinite 'a'
der is a German article, the definite 'the'

indicators.note: ordered means the letters of are are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Foreign lingerie bought by women through a mail order catalogue.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingerie is women's intimate clothing worn beneath outer garments.

clue.text: Aunty in gilet, pockets loosening

indicators.note: pockets means the outer words hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: An aunt in a sleeveless jacket undoes her pockets.
explanation.definitionFit: Undoing knots or ties is a way of making something slacker.

clue.text: Vicious punk rocker returned to get rest for illness

indicators.note: returned means the name is read backwards

parts.note: Sid Vicious was bassist of the Sex Pistols punk band
ease is rest or relaxation

explanation.surface: A wild punk musician comes back to recuperate from sickness.
explanation.definitionFit: A disorder of health in body or mind is a sickness.

clue.text: Rags made from loose dress, first to last

indicators.note: first to last means the opening letter moves to the end

parts.note: a smock is a loose overgarment or dress

explanation.surface: Tatty old clothes fashioned out of a baggy frock.
explanation.definitionFit: To rag someone is to tease or ridicule them, which is to taunt them.

clue.text: Continued briefly with article in house

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut down to its short written abbreviation

parts.note: taken as written, before shortening
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A story keeps going with an item set in a house.
explanation.definitionFit: To house something is to hold or accommodate it within.

clue.text: Mistrust religious school detaining us with pressure

indicators.note: detaining means the group holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a sect is a religious group or school of thought
P is the physics abbreviation for pressure

explanation.surface: We distrust a religious group that holds us under pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: To doubt someone's honesty is to suspect them.

clue.text: Son visits gallery, showing discernment

indicators.note: visits means the letter for son goes into the gallery

parts.note: the Tate is the famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: A cultured son goes to an art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: Good judgement in matters of style and aesthetics is called good taste.

clue.text: In stress, I'd start to show blunders

indicators.note: In tells us the letters of I'd are placed inside the word for stress

parts.note: an accent is stress placed on a syllable
taken as written, without the apostrophe

indicators.note: start to means just the opening letter of show

explanation.surface: Someone under pressure admits they are beginning to make mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Mishaps and mistakes made unintentionally are both kinds of blunders.

clue.text: Winning as a captain?

parts.note: a captain is a head or leader

explanation.surface: Is a team ahead because of its captain?
explanation.definitionFit: A side that is in the lead is in front of its rivals.

clue.text: Sketch daughter on flat wooden boat

parts.note: a raft is a flat floating platform of wood

explanation.surface: A girl draws a picture while sitting on a raft.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough preliminary version or outline is an early drawing.

clue.text: Judge from one American state impounding 1000 dollars

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: impounding means the state holds the sum inside it

parts.note: Maine is a US state in New England
G, a grand, is slang for a thousand dollars

explanation.surface: A judge from a US state seizes a large fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judge' is a verb here: to suppose or reckon.
explanation.definitionFit: To judge that something is so is to suppose or suspect it, a looser sense of picturing.

clue.text: Not informed United Nations has a battle with Spain

parts.note: war is armed conflict, a battle
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: The UN, kept in the dark, finds itself fighting Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ignorant of a fact has not been told or is oblivious to it.

clue.text: Fancied lodger? Sounds like it

indicators.note: Sounds like it says the word for lodger is heard, matching the written answer

parts.note: a paying guest is a lodger

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they were attracted to the lodger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancied' looks like 'was attracted to' but means supposed.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy that something is so is to suppose it, a conjecture.

clue.text: Nice text — unfortunately line finally goes dead

indicators.note: unfortunately means the letters of nice text are in a sorry, jumbled state
finally means the closing letter of line, which goes out of the mix

explanation.surface: A pleasant message ends badly when the last line disappears.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange NICETEXT after the E from the end of 'line' 'goes', leaving the seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A species that has died out completely is no longer living anywhere.
